meta.condition_grammar: A 'when' is a list of clauses that must ALL be true. Clause: {"var": name, "op": one of eq|ne|in|lt|lte|gt|gte|set|unset, "value": ...}. A 'route' is evaluated top to bottom; the first entry whose 'when' passes wins; an entry with no 'when' is the default.
meta.text_tokens: {{name}} inside text is replaced by a variable or computed value (see SPEC.md 'Computed values'). {{fact:id}} renders the fact's plain text with its label badge and source link. {{fact:id.value.path}} renders one value with badge and link.
meta.tone: Plain English, short sentences, second person ('you'), for a 67-year-old non-expert. No jargon without the glossary pop-up.

part_a_date.note: Part A start (entitlement) month from the Medicare card

job_cov_end.default_rule: last day of last_work_month (fact his_coverage_end_assumption, ASSUMED)

wife_birth.note: day matters only if it is the 1st

magi_by_tax_year.note: joint MAGI estimates keyed by tax year 2025-2030

one_time_income.note: Roth conversions + capital gains included in that year's MAGI

nodes.text: Do you have a Medicare card that says HOSPITAL (PART A)?

options.label: No, I have no Medicare card

nodes.intro: Answer a few short questions. You get a to-do list with dates.

nodes.text: Does your company have 20 or more employees?
nodes.help: If yes, your job plan pays first. If not, Medicare pays first. HR knows the number Medicare uses.

nodes.title: Medicare probably pays first for you now
nodes.text: Your company has fewer than 20 employees, so Medicare pays first and your job plan pays second. You may need Part B now. Waiting could mean a late penalty and bills your job plan won't pay. Call NJ SHIP this week.
more: {{fact:employer_size_20}}
Much of this guide assumes a larger company, so check with NJ SHIP before relying on it.

nodes.text: When do you plan to stop working? A guess is fine.
nodes.default_note: We assume your job health plan ends on the last day of that month.

nodes.text: On what day does your job health plan end?
Is your wife covered by your job's health plan right now?
When was your wife born? Pick the month and year.
nodes.first_label: She was born on the 1st of the month

nodes.text: What Part A start date is on your card?
nodes.help: This date matters for how long your wife can keep COBRA. If you can't find it, choose 'I don't know' and we'll add it to your questions for Social Security.

nodes.text: Does the same card also say MEDICAL (PART B)?
What start date is printed next to MEDICAL (PART B)?
After you retire, will your company still give you health coverage?
nodes.help: This is called retiree coverage. It is not COBRA. COBRA lasts a short time and usually costs a lot.

nodes.text: Does your wife's own employer offer her a health plan she could join?
Each year your job plan sends a letter about drug coverage. Does it say the coverage is "creditable"?
nodes.help: Plans send this notice every year, often in the fall. It protects you from the Part D late penalty while you work.

nodes.title: Your drug coverage may not protect you from the Part D penalty
nodes.text: If your job plan's drug coverage is not creditable, a Part D late penalty may already be building for each month without it. Ask NJ SHIP soon how and when you can join a Medicare drug plan.
more: {{fact:creditable_notice}}
{{fact:partd_penalty}}

nodes.title: You already have Part B while working
nodes.text: Your job plan pays first, so Part B mostly pays second. You pay {{fig:partb_premium}} a month or more for it.

variants.text: Your one-time Medigap window started when Part B started ({{part_b_date}}) and {{medigap_window_status}}.
We can't tell when your one-time Medigap window was, because your Part B start date is unknown. Ask NJ SHIP (question below).

more: {{fact:employer_size_20}}
If your Medigap window has already closed: the federal guaranteed right to buy Medigap does NOT apply when a job plan that pays first ends. {{fact:gi_primary_plan_not_federal}}
New Jersey's own rule appears to give a broader right when you leave a job plan that pays first. {{fact:gi_nj_state_extension}}

Dropping Part B now saves the premium, and you can sign up again later without penalty while you work. {{fact:partb_defer_while_working}} It does NOT give you a new Medigap window. {{fact:medigap_oep}}

nodes.text: Do you or your company put money into a Health Savings Account (HSA)?
nodes.help: Look for "HSA" on your pay stub. No HSA money can go in for months you have Medicare, even backdated months.

nodes.title: HSA contributions and Medicare
nodes.text: No HSA money may go in for any month you have Medicare. Money put in for those months counts as an excess contribution.

variants.text: Part A is backdated when you sign up (see below), so this reaches back to months you have already worked. Talk to HR (and a tax adviser) before you sign up.
You already have Medicare, so no HSA money may go in now. Ask HR to stop contributions, and ask a tax adviser about removing any excess.
You weren't sure whether HSA money goes in for you. Find out from HR soon.

more: {{fact:parta_retro}}
{{fact:hsa_medicare}}

nodes.title: Part A: when to sign up
nodes.text: Most people pay nothing for Part A.

variants.text: Sign up by {{parta_signup_by}}. Part A will then start about {{part_a_projected_start}}, because it is backdated. If your wife is on your plan, her COBRA could then last until about {{wife_cobra_end_if_parta_now}}, if you stop working by {{retire_by_for_36}}. Ask your plan to confirm.

Part A is backdated to a start before the month you sign up, and that start date sets how long your wife can keep COBRA. Signing up now would be too early to help her. Sign up between {{parta_signup_earliest_for_36}} and {{parta_signup_latest_for_36}} instead. The later you sign up in that time, the longer her COBRA: up to about {{wife_cobra_end_if_parta_latest}}, instead of {{wife_cobra_end}}. Confirm with the plan administrator and Social Security before choosing a month.
Your wife's regular COBRA already reaches her Medicare start, so when you sign up for Part A doesn't change her coverage.
Your wife isn't on your job plan, so the COBRA timing doesn't apply to her.
HSA: no money can go in for any month you have Part A, even backdated months. Talk to HR before you sign up.

more: Part A (hospital insurance) has no monthly premium for most people with enough work history. {{fact:parta_premium_free}} When you sign up also decides how long your wife can keep COBRA, as explained below.
{{fact:parta_retro}}
Part A pays second to your job plan on hospital bills. {{fact:employer_size_20}}
It can lengthen your wife's COBRA if your Part A start date is less than 18 months before you stop working. {{fact:cobra_36_month_rule}}

nodes.title: While you work, you can wait for Part B
nodes.text: If your company has 20 or more employees, your job plan pays first. Then you can wait to get Part B until your job or your job health plan ends, with no late penalty. Keep the yearly drug letter from your plan.

variants.text: You were not sure about 20 employees. Ask HR this month.
Your company has fewer than 20 employees, so this may not apply to you. Call NJ SHIP.
Get the yearly drug letter before you rely on these dates.
Your drug coverage may not be "creditable". See the earlier warning.

more: {{fact:partb_defer_while_working}}
{{fact:employer_size_20}}
Keep the yearly 'creditable coverage' letter from your plan. {{fact:creditable_notice}}
Medicare Open Enrollment does not apply to you unless you already have a Medicare drug or Advantage plan. {{fact:medicare_oep}}

nodes.title: You have retiree coverage: check it before choosing anything else
nodes.text: After you retire, Medicare pays first and your retiree plan pays second. Many retiree plans won't pay unless you have both Part A and Part B. Joining an outside Medigap, drug or Advantage plan could cost you (and your wife) the retiree coverage.
more: {{fact:retiree_coverage_check}}
Ask whether retiree coverage includes your wife before she turns 65. That could solve her bridge.

nodes.title: Find out about retiree coverage first
nodes.text: Ask HR if there is any retiree health coverage. Until you know, this guide assumes there is none (our guess).

nodes.comment: Uses computed values bridge_months and wife_cobra_end (SPEC.md).

nodes.title: Your retirement doesn't change your wife's coverage
nodes.text: She isn't on your job plan, so nothing ends for her when you retire.

variants.text: If she has no health coverage now, she can buy a plan through Get Covered NJ during open enrollment.

more: {{fact:gcnj_oe_2027}}

nodes.title: No gap for your wife
nodes.text: Your job coverage lasts until her Medicare starts ({{wife_medicare_start}}). She needs no bridge coverage.

variants.text: She will already be on Medicare when your job coverage ends. Like you, she must sign up for Part B and join a drug plan before your job coverage ends, so she has no gap or penalty. Her Part B can start {{wife_partb_start}}, and her own 6-month Medigap window then runs to {{wife_medigap_window_close}}.

more: {{fact:partb_sep}}

nodes.title: COBRA can cover your wife until her Medicare starts
nodes.text: Your job health plan ends {{job_cov_end}}. COBRA can cover her until {{wife_cobra_end}}. Her Medicare starts {{wife_medicare_start}}. Ask HR what COBRA costs for her alone. Compare it with a Get Covered NJ plan. Choose one when your plan ends. If she starts COBRA and stops it early, she can switch only in open enrollment.
more: How long COBRA lasts for her: {{wife_cobra_rule}}.
{{fact:cobra_basics}}
Ask HR for her single-coverage COBRA price now. The COBRA fact above says the most it can cost.
Compare that price with a Get Covered NJ plan. Losing your job plan opens a special window for her to enroll there. {{fact:gcnj_sep_loss}}
Choose between COBRA and Get Covered NJ when your job plan ends. If she starts COBRA and drops it early, she can't switch to Get Covered NJ until open enrollment. {{fact:cobra_drop_no_sep}}

nodes.text: After you retire and before your wife turns 65, what will your yearly household income be?
nodes.help: These lines are for 2027 coverage. Poverty lines change each year, so the lines for later years will differ. {{fact:fpl_lines_household2}} {{fact:aca_magi_includes_ss}}
nodes.subtext: Count all of it: pensions, IRA money, investment gains, and all Social Security, even the part that is not taxed.

nodes.title: Your wife needs about {{cobra_gap_months}} months of other coverage
nodes.text: COBRA can cover her until {{wife_cobra_end}}. Her Medicare starts {{wife_medicare_start}}. For the months between, she can use her own job plan, if she has one. Or she can buy a Get Covered NJ plan. Or you can work longer. If she gets help with the price and your income ends up higher than you guessed, you pay back the extra.

variants.text: At this income she may get help with the price from the U.S. and from New Jersey.
At this income she may get New Jersey help, but no U.S. help.
At this income she pays full price on Get Covered NJ.
Her price depends on your income in those years. Below {{fact:fpl_lines_household2.value.pct600}} she may get New Jersey help; below {{fact:fpl_lines_household2.value.pct400}}, federal help too.

more: {{fact:nj_health_plan_savings}}
{{fact:federal_ptc_400_cliff}}
Options: (1) work longer so the gap shrinks; (2) her own employer's plan, if offered; (3) Get Covered NJ; (4) a mix: COBRA first, then Get Covered NJ when COBRA runs out.
If she gets advance tax credits and your income comes in higher than you estimated, you must repay all of the extra. {{fact:ptc_full_repayment}}
If her own employer offers affordable coverage, she can't get marketplace credits. {{fact:employer_offer_blocks_ptc}}
Income from Roth conversions, gains and IRA withdrawals in these years raises her marketplace price in the same year.
If she later leaves her own small employer's plan, New Jersey's state continuation may apply to that plan. {{fact:nj_mini_cobra}}
Choose between COBRA and Get Covered NJ when your job plan ends. If she starts COBRA and drops it early, she can't switch to Get Covered NJ until open enrollment. {{fact:cobra_drop_no_sep}}

nodes.title: When your wife turns 65 ({{wife_medicare_start}})
nodes.text: If she is still on your job plan and you still work, she can wait for Part B. If she is on COBRA or a Get Covered NJ plan, she should sign up for Parts A and B in the 7 months around her 65th birthday month. COBRA does not protect her from the Part B late penalty. She needs her own Medigap or Advantage plan; yours does not cover her.
more: Which plan pays first for her at 65 depends on where her coverage comes from.
If she is on your plan and you are still working at a 20+ employer: your plan pays first, and she can wait for Part B. {{fact:partb_defer_while_working}}
If her coverage is from her own employer with fewer than 20 workers: Medicare pays first. She should sign up for Parts A and B when first eligible. {{fact:employer_size_20}}
If she is on COBRA or a marketplace plan: she should sign up for Medicare in her Initial Enrollment Period. {{fact:iep_window}} COBRA does not protect her from the Part B penalty. {{fact:partb_sep}}
Her own one-time Medigap window starts when her Part B starts. She needs her own policy. {{fact:medigap_needs_ab_no_drugs}}
Once she is on Medicare, IRMAA applies to her too, and she files her own SSA-44. {{fact:lce_reporter_only}}

nodes.title: Your Medicare sign-up timeline
nodes.text: Your job health plan ends {{job_cov_end}}. Dates are estimates from your answers.

timeline.text: Apply for Part B. Ask for it to start {{partb_start}}. HR signs form CMS-L564.
timeline.detail: Ask HR to sign Form CMS-L564. Apply for Part B online at SSA or with Form CMS-40B. Ask for Part B to start {{partb_start}}. {{fact:partb_forms}} {{fact:partb_sep_start_date}}

timeline.text: Earliest day to join a Medicare Advantage plan, only if you want one.
timeline.detail: Earliest date to apply for a Medicare Advantage plan, if you choose one. {{fact:ma_window_new_to_b}}

timeline.text: Join a Medicare drug plan (or an Advantage plan with drugs) by this day. Then it starts {{partb_start}}, with no gap.
timeline.detail: Join a Medicare drug plan (or an Advantage plan with drug coverage) by this date so it starts {{partb_start}}, right after your job coverage ends. {{fact:partd_sep_effective_date}}

timeline.text: Part B starts. Your one-time 6-month Medigap window opens. No health questions in this window.
timeline.detail: Part B starts. Your one-time 6-month Medigap window opens. {{fact:medigap_oep}}

timeline.text: Last day to join a drug plan with no lifetime penalty. After {{drug_enroll_by_no_gap}}, you will have some days with no drug coverage.
timeline.detail: Last day to join a drug plan without a lifetime Part D penalty. Joining after {{drug_enroll_by_no_gap}} still leaves weeks with no drug coverage. {{fact:partd_penalty}}

timeline.text: Last day to join an Advantage or drug plan in this window.
timeline.detail: Your window to join a Medicare Advantage or drug plan closes. {{fact:ma_pd_sep_employer_loss}}

timeline.text: Last day to buy Medigap with no health questions. After this, New Jersey companies can say no, unless you have a special right.
timeline.detail: Last day to buy Medigap with no health questions. After this, NJ companies can turn you down. {{fact:nj_underwriting_after_window}}

timeline.text: Very last day to sign up for Part B. After this you may pay a penalty for life and have months with no coverage. COBRA does not give you more time.
timeline.detail: Absolute last day of your 8-month Part B window. Missing it means a lifetime penalty and possibly months with no coverage. COBRA does not extend it. {{fact:partb_sep}} {{fact:partb_penalty}} If missed: {{fact:gep}}

nodes.title: You already have Part B: what changes at retirement
nodes.text: You don't need to sign up again. Your Medigap window {{medigap_window_status}}. Join a Medicare drug or Advantage plan by {{drug_enroll_by_no_gap}}, so it starts with no gap. Last day with no penalty: {{drug_enroll_by_no_penalty}}.

variants.text: A New Jersey rule may give you 63 days after your job plan ends to buy some Medigap plans, until about {{nj_gi_window_close}} (not confirmed). Ask NJ SHIP before you rely on it.

more: {{fact:gi_nj_state_extension}}

Drug coverage: join a Medicare drug or Advantage plan by {{drug_enroll_by_no_gap}} so it starts right after your job coverage ends. The last day to join without a Part D penalty is {{drug_enroll_by_no_penalty}}. {{fact:partd_sep_effective_date}} {{fact:partd_penalty}}
If your Medigap window has closed, NJ companies can ask health questions. {{fact:nj_underwriting_after_window}} {{fact:gi_primary_plan_not_federal}} {{fact:gi_nj_state_extension}}

One option to keep a Medigap right: take COBRA for yourself after retiring. Because you already have Medicare, COBRA pays second, and when COBRA ends you get a guaranteed right to buy Medigap. {{fact:gi_after_cobra}} {{fact:cobra_medicare_before_election}} (Cost tradeoff: full COBRA premium. Confirm with NJ SHIP.)
{{fact:gi_63_days}}

nodes.title: Two ways to get Medicare
nodes.text: Way 1: Original Medicare, plus Medigap, plus a drug plan. You can see any doctor who takes Medicare. It costs more each month, with few surprise bills. Way 2: Medicare Advantage. A private plan with a network of doctors. It often costs less each month. You pay copays, up to {{fig:ma_moop.in_network}} a year in the network. With both ways, you still pay for Part B.
more: {{fact:ma_requires_partb}}
The next few questions weigh cost, keeping your doctors, and predictable bills equally.

nodes.text: Do you see a specialist often, have a long-term health problem, or expect surgery in the next few years?
nodes.help: This answer is never saved. It only helps compare the two ways.

nodes.text: How important is it to see any doctor or hospital that takes Medicare, with no referral?

options.label: Not important. A local network is fine.

nodes.subtext: For example, big hospitals in New York City or Philadelphia.

nodes.text: Do you spend weeks at a time outside New Jersey?
Which do you prefer?

options.label: Pay more each month, with almost no surprise bills
Pay less each month, but some years have bills of a few thousand dollars

nodes.text: In June 2026, Medigap Plan G cost about {{fact:nj_medigap_rates_jun2026.value.plan_g.low}} to {{fact:nj_medigap_rates_jun2026.value.plan_g.high}} a month at age 65 in New Jersey. At your age it costs more. You also need a drug plan. Can you pay that?

nodes.comment: Scoring rules in SPEC.md 'Medigap vs Advantage scoring'.

nodes.title: Your answers point to Original Medicare and Medigap
nodes.text: You also need a drug plan. Buy Medigap in your 6-month window: {{partb_start}} to {{medigap_window_close}}. After that, New Jersey companies can ask health questions and say no.

variants.text: Your one-time window is open now, while your job plan still pays first. Buying Medigap now means paying for it about {{months_until_retire}} months before you need it, but it locks in no health questions. Ask NJ SHIP before deciding.

more: You put weight on choosing doctors and on predictable bills. Leaving Medigap later is easy; getting back in may not be.
{{fact:medigap_oep}}
{{fact:nj_underwriting_after_window}}
You also need a separate drug plan. {{fact:medigap_needs_ab_no_drugs}}

nodes.title: Your answers point to Medicare Advantage
nodes.text: Check that your doctors are in the plan's network. This choice is hard to undo. If you want Medigap later, New Jersey companies can ask health questions and say no. A trial right to switch back probably does not apply to you (our reading of the rule). Ask NJ SHIP.
more: Worst case in a bad year: up to {{fig:ma_moop.in_network}} in-network for medical care, plus drug costs up to {{fig:partd_limits.oop_cap}}.
Check that your doctors and hospitals are in the plan's network on Medicare.gov Plan Finder. Networks can change each year.
{{fact:nj_underwriting_after_window}}

At your age you would likely have no trial right to switch back to Medigap with guaranteed acceptance, so treat joining Advantage as hard to undo. Ask NJ SHIP (question below). {{fact:ma_trial_right_at_your_age}}
{{fact:ma_oep}}

nodes.title: It is a close call
nodes.text: Your answers point both ways. Get free help: book a meeting with NJ SHIP. Bring your doctor list and drug list. Remember: Medigap is the choice that is hard to get back into.
more: {{fact:nj_underwriting_after_window}}
{{fact:nj_ship_contact}}

nodes.title: Your 6-month Medigap window has passed
nodes.text: New Jersey companies can now ask about your health and say no. You can still apply. A New Jersey rule may give you 63 days after your job plan ends to buy some plans (not confirmed). Ask NJ SHIP soon.

variants.text: That would be until about {{nj_gi_window_close}}.

more: NJ companies can now look at your health and say no or charge more. You can still apply; if a company accepts you, the policy works the same. Otherwise Medicare Advantage is open to you during your enrollment windows.
{{fact:nj_underwriting_after_window}}
{{fact:gi_primary_plan_not_federal}}
{{fact:gi_nj_state_extension}}
{{fact:gi_after_cobra}}

nodes.text: In a typical year, how many doctor visits do you have?
nodes.help: Plans G, N and High-Deductible G all pay big hospital bills the same way. They differ in small, frequent costs.

nodes.text: If a big medical bill came, could you pay up to {{fig:hdg_deductible}} yourself before the plan pays?
Do all your doctors "take assignment"? That means they accept Medicare's price as full payment.
nodes.help: Ask each office: 'Do you accept Medicare assignment?' If a doctor doesn't, they can bill up to 15% more. Plan G pays that; Plan N doesn't.

nodes.title: Plan G fits your answers best
nodes.text: Plan G fits your answers best. It pays almost all costs Medicare leaves to you, except the Part B deductible ({{fig:partb_deductible}}). Every company's Plan G has the same benefits. So compare the price, and how fast the price went up.
more: {{fact:plan_g_benefits}}
{{fact:plans_cf_closed}}
Every company's Plan G has the same benefits. Shop on price and on how fast the price has risen. {{fact:nj_premium_changes}}

nodes.title: Plan N could save money; compare it with Plan G
nodes.text: Plan N costs less each month. You pay small copays and any excess charges. Enter real quotes below to see which costs less for your number of visits.
more: {{fact:plan_n_differences}}
{{fact:plan_g_benefits}}

nodes.title: High-Deductible Plan G could save money
nodes.text: Its premium is much lower ({{fact:nj_medigap_rates_jun2026.value.hd_plan_g.low}} to {{fact:nj_medigap_rates_jun2026.value.hd_plan_g.high}} a month at 65). You pay the first {{fig:hdg_deductible}} each year yourself, then it works like Plan G.
more: {{fact:hdg_deductible}}
Compare: yearly premium savings vs. the deductible you might pay in a bad year.

nodes.title: Will your income raise your Medicare premiums?
nodes.text: Medicare charges more when income is high. It usually looks at your tax return from 2 years before. So your last working years can raise your first Medicare costs. Enter your expected joint income for each year.
more: {{fact:irmaa_lookback}}

nodes.title: How to lower income-based charges
nodes.text: When you stop working, you can ask Social Security to use your new, lower income. Use form SSA-44. One-time income, like a Roth conversion or a big sale of stock, cannot be lowered this way.
more: Retiring is a 'work stoppage', one of the 8 events that let you ask Social Security to use your newer, lower income.
{{fact:lce_list}}
{{fact:lce_attestation}}
{{fact:lce_effective}}
{{fact:lce_nonqualifying}} So in the years that set your premiums, large Roth conversions or sales with big gains can't be appealed.
{{fact:lce_spouse_event}} {{fact:lce_reporter_only}}
{{fact:ssa44_form}}

Social Security timing: waiting past full retirement age raises your check (see source) and keeps it out of your income for now. Once you start it, the taxable part counts toward IRMAA income and all of it counts toward your wife's marketplace income. {{fact:ss_delayed_credits}} {{fact:aca_magi_includes_ss}}

nodes.title: Your next steps
nodes.text: Print this page. Bring it to HR, Social Security and NJ SHIP.
Next: pick a plan type. It takes a few quick questions.

options.label: Not now. Show my to-do list

nodes.title: Choose a plan type later, with free help
nodes.text: Book a free NJ SHIP meeting to choose between Medigap and Medicare Advantage. Until you choose, your to-do list has no Medigap price steps. You can come back and choose at any time.

variants.text: If you want Medigap, decide before your Medigap window closes on {{medigap_window_close}}. After that, New Jersey companies can ask about your health and say no.

nodes.text: Optional: check whether your income will raise your Medicare costs.

ACT_GET_CREDITABLE_LETTER.text: Get this year's 'creditable prescription drug coverage' letter from your plan and keep it. Do this before relying on this guide's drug-plan timing.
ACT_GET_CREDITABLE_LETTER.short: Get your plan's yearly drug letter. Keep it.

ACT_HR_QUESTIONS.text: Ask HR the questions on the HR list below.
ACT_HR_QUESTIONS.short: Ask HR the questions on your HR list.

ACT_ASK_HR_PARTA_OK.when_text: Next 2 weeks, before signing up for Part A
ACT_ASK_HR_PARTA_OK.text: Confirm with HR that having Part A doesn't change your job plan.
ACT_ASK_HR_PARTA_OK.short: Ask HR: does getting Part A change my job plan?

ACT_ENROLL_PARTA.text: Sign up for Part A only at ssa.gov/medicare/sign-up. Note the start date on your card.
ACT_ENROLL_PARTA.short: Sign up for Part A only, at ssa.gov/medicare/sign-up.

ACT_SHIP_PARTB_ALREADY.text: Call NJ SHIP about keeping or dropping Part B while working, and about your Medigap rights at retirement.
ACT_SHIP_PARTB_ALREADY.short: Call NJ SHIP: should you keep Part B while you work?

ACT_BOOK_SHIP.text: Book a free NJ SHIP session. Bring your doctor list and prescriptions.
ACT_BOOK_SHIP.short: Book a free NJ SHIP meeting. Bring your doctor and drug lists.

ACT_PARTB_FILE.text: Get Form CMS-L564 signed by HR. Apply for Part B (online at SSA or Form CMS-40B) with a start date of {{partb_start}}.
ACT_PARTB_FILE.short: Apply for Part B. Ask for it to start {{partb_start}}.

ACT_PLAN_SHOP.text: Compare drug plans (and Advantage plans, if considering) on Medicare.gov Plan Finder with your exact prescriptions.
ACT_PLAN_SHOP.short: Compare drug plans on Medicare.gov Plan Finder, using your exact drugs.

ACT_MEDIGAP_QUOTES.text: Get Medigap quotes at your age from several NJ companies. Ask how each prices by age and its recent increases. Apply so the policy starts with Part B.
ACT_MEDIGAP_QUOTES.short: Get Medigap prices from several New Jersey companies.

ACT_SSA44.when_text: After your last day of work: when the IRMAA letter arrives, or in January of your first Medicare year
ACT_SSA44.text: File Form SSA-44 for 'work stoppage' with an estimate of this year's and next year's income. Repeat for the second year if needed.
ACT_SSA44.short: After you stop working, send form SSA-44 so Social Security can use your lower income.

ACT_WIFE_COBRA_ELECT.when_text: About 60 days after your coverage ends (the COBRA notice gives the exact deadline)
ACT_WIFE_COBRA_ELECT.text: Your wife elects COBRA (or enrolls in another plan) so she has no gap.
ACT_WIFE_COBRA_ELECT.short: Your wife signs up for COBRA or another plan. The COBRA letter gives the deadline.

ACT_PRICE_GCNJ.when_text: During Get Covered NJ open enrollment before you retire
ACT_PRICE_GCNJ.text: Use Get Covered NJ's Shop and Compare tool to price plans for your wife at her age and your expected income.
ACT_PRICE_GCNJ.short: Check Get Covered NJ prices for your wife.

ACT_WIFE_GCNJ_ENROLL.when_text: Within 60 days before or after her COBRA ends
ACT_WIFE_GCNJ_ENROLL.text: Your wife enrolls in a Get Covered NJ plan.
ACT_WIFE_GCNJ_ENROLL.short: Your wife joins a Get Covered NJ plan, so she has no gap when COBRA ends.

ACT_WIFE_MEDICARE_SIGNUP.text: Your wife signs up for Medicare Parts A and B (unless she is still on your job plan while you work), then picks Medigap + drug plan or Advantage in her own windows.
ACT_WIFE_MEDICARE_SIGNUP.short: Your wife signs up for Medicare A and B, unless she is still on your job plan while you work.

ACT_ENROLL_PARTA_WINDOW.text: Sign up for Part A only, at ssa.gov/medicare/sign-up. The later you sign up in this time, the longer your wife's COBRA can last. If her regular COBRA already reaches her Medicare start, the month doesn't matter for her. Ask the plan administrator to confirm first, and note the start date on your card.
ACT_ENROLL_PARTA_WINDOW.short: Sign up for Part A only. The later in this time, the longer your wife's COBRA.

ACT_MEDIGAP_APPLY.when_text: About a month before Part B starts
ACT_MEDIGAP_APPLY.text: Apply for your Medigap policy so it starts {{partb_start}}, the day your Part B starts.
ACT_MEDIGAP_APPLY.short: Apply for Medigap so it starts {{partb_start}}, with your Part B.

ACT_MEDIGAP_QUOTES_HAS_B.when_text: At least 2 months before your Medigap window closes ({{medigap_window_close}})
ACT_MEDIGAP_QUOTES_HAS_B.text: After talking with NJ SHIP, get Medigap quotes from several NJ companies and decide before your window closes.
ACT_MEDIGAP_QUOTES_HAS_B.short: Get Medigap prices and decide before {{medigap_window_close}}.

ACT_ENROLL_DRUG.text: Join a Medicare drug plan (or an Advantage plan with drug coverage) so it starts right after your job coverage ends ({{job_cov_end}} is the last day). Join no later than {{drug_enroll_by_no_penalty}}, or a lifetime Part D penalty applies.
ACT_ENROLL_DRUG.short: Join a Medicare drug plan so it starts with no gap. Final no-penalty day: {{drug_enroll_by_no_penalty}}.

ACT_NJ_GI_CONFIRM.when_text: 3 months before your job coverage ends
ACT_NJ_GI_CONFIRM.text: Ask NJ SHIP which Medigap plans New Jersey's 63-day right lets you buy when your job plan ends (until about {{nj_gi_window_close}}).
ACT_NJ_GI_CONFIRM.short: Ask NJ SHIP which Medigap plans New Jersey's 63-day right covers (not confirmed).

ACT_WIFE_PARTB_FILE.text: Your wife applies for Part B (Form CMS-40B, with her own CMS-L564 signed by your HR) with a start date of {{wife_partb_start}}.
ACT_WIFE_PARTB_FILE.short: Your wife applies for Part B, to start {{wife_partb_start}}.

ACT_WIFE_DRUG.text: Your wife joins her own Medicare drug plan (or an Advantage plan with drug coverage) so it starts right after your job coverage ends.
ACT_WIFE_DRUG.short: Your wife joins her own Medicare drug plan.

ACT_SHIP_NOW.text: Call NJ SHIP: with fewer than 20 employees, Medicare may already pay first for you.
ACT_SHIP_NOW.short: Call NJ SHIP ({{fact:nj_ship_contact.value}}) this week. Medicare may already pay first for you.

ACT_SHIP_DRUG_NOW.text: Ask NJ SHIP whether your drug coverage counts as creditable, and when you can join a Medicare drug plan.
ACT_SHIP_DRUG_NOW.short: Ask NJ SHIP: does your drug coverage count as "creditable"?

ACT_HR_EMPLOYEES.text: Ask HR how many employees the company counts for Medicare, and whether its plan pays before Medicare for you.
ACT_HR_EMPLOYEES.short: Ask HR: does the company have 20 or more employees, for Medicare?

Q_HR_EMPLOYEES.text: How many employees does the company count for Medicare purposes? Does our plan pay before Medicare for me?

Q_HR_CREDITABLE.text: Can I have the written notice that our drug coverage is creditable?

Q_HR_RETIREE_DETAILS.text: Is there retiree medical coverage for me and my wife? Does it require Parts A and B? Would joining Medigap, a drug plan or Medicare Advantage end it?

Q_HR_COVERAGE_END.text: If my last day is in a given month, on what exact date does my health coverage end?

Q_HR_COBRA_COST.text: What will COBRA cost per month for my wife alone?

Q_HR_COBRA_36.text: If my Part A start (entitlement) date is {{his_entitlement}}, how long can my wife keep COBRA? Please confirm the 36-month rule in writing.

Q_HR_L564.text: Who signs Form CMS-L564 for me, and how long does it take?

Q_HR_PAYOUTS.text: Can severance, bonus or unused-vacation pay be paid in a particular tax year?

Q_SHIP_TIMING.text: Given my Part A and B status, on what date should my Part B start?

Q_SHIP_GI_PRIMARY.text: My Medigap window has passed. Does New Jersey give me a guaranteed right to buy Medigap when my job plan (which pays before Medicare) ends? Would taking COBRA first give me that right when COBRA ends?

Q_SHIP_DROP_B.text: Should I keep Part B while I'm still working, or drop it and re-enroll at retirement?

Q_SHIP_PRICING.text: Which NJ Medigap companies raise prices with age, and what were their recent rate increases?

Q_SHIP_TRIAL.text: If I try Medicare Advantage first at my age, do I have any right to switch back to Medigap later?

Q_SHIP_NETWORK.text: Which Advantage plans include my doctors and hospitals?

Q_SSA_STATUS.text: What is my Part A start (entitlement) date? Am I enrolled in Part B?

Q_SSA_SEP.text: If I file for Part B before my last day of work, can it start the first day after my job coverage ends?

Q_SSA_44.text: What proof of work stoppage do you want with Form SSA-44? Can I file before I receive an IRMAA notice?

Q_SSA_SPOUSE_LCE.text: Can my wife's retirement count as my life-changing event?

Q_SSA_CLAIMING.text: If I start Social Security now, how will Part B and IRMAA be taken from my check?

Q_HR_HSA.text: Do I or the company put money into an HSA for me? When can those contributions stop, so none go in for the months my Part A will be backdated?

Q_SSA_PARTA_START.text: If I apply for Part A only, what start date will my card show? If I apply in {{parta_signup_latest_for_36}} instead of now, what start date would I get?

Q_HR_PARTA_ENTITLEMENT.text: Does the plan count my backdated Part A start date as my Medicare entitlement date for my wife's 36-month COBRA rule?

Q_SHIP_NJ_GI_PLANS.text: Which Medigap plans does New Jersey's guaranteed right let me buy when I leave my job plan, and does it include Plan G?

part_a.text: Hospital insurance: hospital stays, nursing care after a hospital stay, and hospice.

part_b.text: Medical insurance: doctors, tests and outpatient care. You pay for it each month.

part_d.text: Insurance for prescription drugs. Private companies sell it.

medigap.text: Extra insurance from a private company. It pays most of what Original Medicare does not pay. Plans have letters, like G and N.

medicare_advantage.text: A private plan you use instead of Original Medicare. It usually has a network of doctors, and copays up to a yearly limit.

irmaa.text: An extra charge on Part B and Part D when your income is high.

cobra.text: A way to keep your job health plan for a while after it ends. You usually pay the full price.

creditable_coverage.text: Drug coverage that is expected to pay at least as much as Medicare's standard drug coverage.

guaranteed_issue.text: A time when a company must sell you Medigap without asking about your health.

take_assignment.text: The doctor accepts Medicare's price as full payment.

ship.text: New Jersey's free Medicare counseling. Counselors do not favor any company.

premium.text: The price you pay each month for insurance.

deductible.text: What you pay each year before the plan starts to pay.

copay.text: A set amount you pay for a visit, like a doctor visit.

network.text: The doctors and hospitals a plan works with.

pays_first.text: The plan that pays your bill first. The other plan may pay part of what is left.

hsa.text: Health Savings Account. A tax-free account for health costs.

gcnj.text: New Jersey's website to buy health insurance.
